content:
**issue-535 chain closed: VCS_TOKEN PR-time governance gate, T7b residual deferred to #551**

What shipped: issue #535 — the PR-time governance gate authenticated through the GitHub-only GH_TOKEN. It worked only by accident: with no VCS_TOKEN set, nothing binds and `gh` picks up the ambient GH_TOKEN, so a GitLab consumer would have received six required jobs wired to a credential their provider never reads. GH_TOKEN is now fully removed from the three port-reaching steps, never left alongside VCS_TOKEN.

The ticket's premise was partly wrong: `issue-link` (governance.yml:54) had ALREADY been fixed by #479, so three steps needed the GH_TOKEN → VCS_TOKEN swap, not four. The measurement corrected the ticket during implementation.

Second half of the work: `auditWorkflowAuth` now resolves port-reach PER INVOCATION rather than per file, via a SUBCOMMAND_PORT_REACH manifest declared in run-check.mjs and read as TEXT — never imported, because importing it would make the guard the first violator of the "run-check.mjs is an entry point, never a library" invariant it enforces. governance.yml joined the audited workflow set. The permissions: regex used to match only flow style while governance.yml uses block style, so condition 2 was silently unevaluated — fixed. A further residual closed in PR D (#550): permissionsScopes() also collapsed "permissions: header present but zero scope lines" (a block of only comments, or flow-style `permissions: {}`) into the same null as "no permissions: key at all", silently skipping the pull-requests-scope check for the most restrictive possible grant — now returns '' (present, empty) to stay distinguishable.

Real-run evidence (the #475 bar): actor-check, brain-writes-reviewed, and issue-link all went green on the chain's own PR runs, authenticating through VCS_TOKEN with no GH_TOKEN present. Note explicitly that diff-size going green is NOT evidence — loadGithubContext swallows prView failures (ci-context.mjs:74) and leaves labels = null, so a small diff passes even with a broken credential.

Delivery: 861 changed lines against a 400-line lite budget, shipped as a feature-branch chain of four PRs, each under budget, cut at prefix boundaries with no commit reordering (reordering conflicts in workflow-auth.test.mjs). Suite verified green at every cut point: 3096 / 3108 / 3119, and PR D's own cut point at 3122 (69+6=75 changed lines).

Review: sdd-verify returned PASS WITH WARNINGS (both closed). Then three rounds of dual blind adversarial review found, in sequence: a fail-open where a YAML comment as the first line under block-style permissions: silently disabled the pull-requests check; a new FALSE caveat in the very comment block this change rewrote (it claimed a corrupt manifest resolves to unresolvable when it actually falls back to the D2 whole-file rule); then two independent vacuous-pass routes in the test (T7b, in run-check.test.mjs) written to close the previous round's finding; then a THIRD route in the same test.

The lesson worth carrying: every one of those three T7b routes is the same defect — the test conflates "could not compute a closure" with "computed a closure and found nothing." Extending the regex closed routes 1 and 2 and left route 3 open (an arrow-function or function-expression dispatch handler still falls through bodyClosure and crossFileClosure to an empty '' closure, which trivially agrees with a manifest entry already declared false). The structural fix is fail-loud on a non-computable closure, matching the production guard's own fail-closed polarity, rather than extending the regex a fourth time. Recorded as open follow-up issue #551 ("test(governance): T7b agrees vacuously when a dispatch handler is an arrow function — the third route to the same empty-closure defect"), referenced from PR D (#550).

Open state for the next agent: the chain is PR A #547 (base: tracker feat/issue-535-vcs-token-gate) → PR B #548 (base: PR A's branch feat/issue-535-01-swap-and-foundation) → PR C #549 (base: PR B's branch feat/issue-535-02-per-invocation) → PR D #550 (base: PR C's branch feat/issue-535-03-guard-coverage), all open. The tracker PR targets main, is a DRAFT, and its body contains "Closes #535" — it is the only PR in the chain that targets the default branch. main advanced 4 commits (through #543/#544/#546-equivalent merges) after the chain was branched from eb8810d, so the tracker will need a rebase before it can merge. The merge decision belongs to the maintainer; nothing in this chain should be merged autonomously.

Process note: two blind judges were run mutating the SAME worktree concurrently during the round-3 review and interfered with each other's mutation-proof state; both compensated for it, but future dual reviews need one worktree per judge to avoid this class of interference.
